label: build-40
system: You are a pragmatic solo developer who has shipped consumer apps and been burned by inference bills. You cost things honestly and you have no stake in whether this idea is good. Output JSON only.
user:
Cost this consumer app idea as a real build.

IDEA
{
  "id": 40,
  "title": "Callable Window Brief",
  "unlock": "A background intent is no longer capped at thirty seconds [299] and Focus filters let the app read that the person has come out of Sleep or Work [308], so a prepared brief can be assembled and delivered at the moment a free slot and a friend's waking hours actually overlap, rather than at a fixed time the user guessed at.",
  "pain": "People who care about friends abroad do remember them, but the remembering happens at an hour when calling is impossible and the impulse dies there, and a prompt that lands outside the narrow window when acting is still possible is what causes the miss.",
  "audience": "Parents of under-fives whose closest friends live three or more time zones away",
  "mechanic": "scheduled_digest",
  "wedge": "One forty-second brief each morning naming at most three people whose waking hours overlap a gap already free in your calendar today, with the overlap stated in both clocks and nothing else in it.",
  "moat": "habit_lock",
  "model": "freemium_subscription",
  "loop": "shareable_artifact",
  "kill": [
    "Fewer than 25% of briefs are opened within 30 minutes of delivery by week 4.",
    "Calls or messages actually placed inside a named window stay under 1 per user per week at day 60.",
    "More than 15% of users move the brief time twice or disable it outright, which means the window is being computed wrongly.",
    "Paid conversion below 3% at 90 days."
  ],
  "why_not_obvious": "The obvious suggestion for this audience is a reminder app, but the evidence says the reminder is not missing \u2014 the hour is [250][264]; and unlike the contacts apps that died needing a last-contacted date, the overlap here is arithmetic on time zone and calendar free/busy, both of which the platform does hand over.",
  "why_now": "Longer background execution plus Focus state [299][308] means the overlap can be worked out and delivered at the one hour it is actionable, which is precisely the failure named in [250] and [264]."
}

2026 facts you must use:
- Frontier text inference is about $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.40 out.
- Apple's on-device and Private Cloud Compute models cost $0 in cloud API fees
  for Small Business Program members under 2M lifetime downloads.
- Real-time voice runs $0.005 to $0.018 per minute on cheap stacks and up to
  $0.091 on flagship speech-to-speech. Model choice is the business model.
- Median consumer subscription price is about $10 monthly, $35 yearly.
- Typical paid conversion for a freemium consumer app is 2-4%.

Return JSON:
{
  "stack": "concrete: platform, language, model choice, backend, store",
  "milestones": ["3-6 items, each a shippable week or two of work"],
  "build_cost_usd": <number: real cost to a solo builder using AI assistance>,
  "weeks_to_v1": <number>,
  "inference_cost_user_month": <number: blended cost per ACTIVE user, not per payer>,
  "price_month": <number>,
  "expected_conversion": <number 0-1>,
  "riskiest_technical_assumption": "one sentence",
  "cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption": "one sentence"
}

Be honest. If this needs continuous voice or video generation, say what that
actually costs per active user. An idea that cannot clear its own inference bill
should show that in the numbers, not be flattered.
